the Kubernetes groups, with a middle-dot.stdout:
what is in this workspace -----------------------------------------------------------

  Kubernetes
    Cluster       kind-houston-local
    Namespace     houston-old
    Arrangement   microservices
    Pods          about 9

  MongoDB
    Version          8.0
    Image            mongo:8.0
    Managed by       a plain StatefulSet
    Authentication   none
    This path is houston's own: the official guide documents only the operator,
    which needs MongoDB 6.0+. Add `--mongo-operator` for the documented path, with
    authentication.

  1 - Point kubectl and helm at this cluster
    houston keeps its own kubeconfig so creating a cluster cannot move the context
    you were using. A bare `kubectl` will not see this workspace until it is
    pointed here, and every command below assumes it:
      export KUBECONFIG=<home>/clients/kubernetes/config

  2 - Open the way in
    Rocket.Chat is reached through a port-forward, which is tied to its pod and
    dies with it. This is the one houston started, so run it again if
    http://localhost:3000 stops answering:
      kubectl -n houston-old port-forward deployment/rocketchat-rocketchat 3000:3000

  3 - Look at what is inside
    What is running, what Rocket.Chat is saying, and the values the release was
    installed with:
      kubectl -n houston-old get pods
      kubectl -n houston-old logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=rocketchat -f
      helm -n houston-old get values rocketchat

  Monitoring
    Prometheus and Grafana are shared by the cluster, not installed per workspace:
    this puts one stack in houston-system, and `--off` leaves it up while any
    other workspace still wants it.
      houston monitor --name old

  What works here
    `logs`, `stats`, `env`, `upgrade`, `backup`, `restore`, `seed`, `monitor`,
    `api`, `pat` and `token` all work on this runtime. `stats` needs
    metrics-server in the cluster and says so if it is missing; `env --set`
    refuses and hands over the `helm upgrade` that changes a value.

a scenario preset.stdout:
what is in this workspace -----------------------------------------------------------

  Scenario - oidc
    OIDC needs one host entry so your browser can reach Keycloak at the
    same URL RC's backend uses. Add this line to /etc/hosts (needs sudo):
      127.0.0.1  keycloak
      That entry points at THIS machine, so the browser has to be on it. From
      another machine, re-create with:  --bind 0.0.0.0 --set idp_host=<this host>
      which needs no hosts entry at all.
    Then log in via 'Keycloak (OIDC)' as user1 / user1.
    Keycloak admin console: http://keycloak:8085  (admin/admin, realm 'houston').
